Item Name: 1970s Mid-Century Table Lamp by Heinz-Josef Ohm for Glashütte Limburg, Pair
Description: This Mid-Century table lamp by Heinz-Josef Ohm for Glashütte Limburg is among the few German lighting designs of the late 1970s to receive the iF Design Award. Model 6193, available here as a pair, was produced from 1978 onwards. The glass base is crafted from matte opal glass in a bulbous bottle form, with a tapered neck and an internal light source. The construction is three-armed: the glass body is illuminated from within by a single lamp, while two additional light sources sit beneath the pagoda fabric shade. This separation allows two distinct lighting moods to be created. The matte opal glass diffuses light evenly without harsh contrasts. With an overall height of 70.5 cm including the shade, this opal glass table lamp fits comfortably on chests of drawers, sideboards and side tables. As a pair, both lamps create a symmetrical arrangement that works in the bedroom as well as the living room. The Glashütte Limburg table lamp represents a design language that places material quality and functionality at the forefront. The design was awarded the iF Design Award in 1978, confirming its position within German post-war design history.

This Mid-Century arc floor lamp from the 1960s displays the typical construction of chrome-plated standing lamps of that era: a curved metal shaft of chrome-plated steel that extends far beyond a seating area or table. The shade is executed as a flat hemisphere of white plastic, directed downward. Standing on a round, grey lacquered steel base, the frame provides stable footing. The arc of the shaft follows a smooth curve upward and ends with the shade at a working height that delivers direct downward light. The overall height of 165 cm and a shade diameter of 40 cm define a clearly delineated light cone. The chrome-plated arc lamp occupies minimal floor space, as the weight rests on the base while the arc spans the room above. As a reading light above an armchair or as supplementary lighting in the living room, this 1960s standing lamp from German production serves well. In an interior with Mid-Century furniture, the piece integrates formally; in modern settings, the vintage arc lamp provides a contrasting accent. No manufacturer's mark present. Signs of wear are visible.
